items.item: Presenting task-per-partition parallelism and idle excess instances as two separate reveals, rather than folding them into one, makes clear that the partition count is a hard ceiling on parallelism while extra instances still have genuine value as failover capacity, not processing capacity.

at.step: Reveal: one task per partition, an assignment that never changes

items.item: Backing a local state store with a compacted changelog topic is the exact same mechanism topic 6 covered in the abstract — this topic's framing is deliberately that it's the same idea shown as the thing a real system is actually built on, not a new idea of its own.

at.step: Reveal: local state stores backed by a compacted changelog topic

items.item: A standby replica's value is best understood through the specific cost it eliminates — the replay of a task's entire changelog history — rather than as a vague 'faster recovery' claim; the toy model's own measured speedup makes that specific mechanism concrete.

at.step: Reveal: a warm standby replaces a full replay with a small gap

items.item: The stream-table duality reveal is this topic's center of gravity by design — everything else (tasks, state stores, standbys, exactly-once) is infrastructure in service of that one idea, which is why it's the step this topic's own takeaway and the chapter's cross-topic framing both anchor to.

at.step: Reveal: the stream-table duality

items.item: Naming ksqlDB's licence restriction precisely (excludes a competing SaaS offering, not general commercial use) rather than vaguely ("restricted license") matters because the imprecise version would wrongly suggest ksqlDB can't be run in an ordinary production deployment, which the source directly contradicts.

at.step: Reveal: exactly-once v two, and a rebalance protocol still filling gaps

items.item: This topic's hook (what changes with no cluster at all) and the recap's close (no cluster, just a library) are the same observation made twice — first as an open question, then as the settled answer every reveal in between built toward.

at.step: Hook: a library, not a cluster

items.item: The toy task-assignment, stream-table, and standby-recovery models are deliberately simplified standalone demonstrations, not ports of Kafka Streams' actual StreamsPartitionAssignor or RocksDB-backed state store internals, and every figure shown is this run's own measured output, not a cited Kafka benchmark.

at.step: Prove it

items.item: This topic uses topic 24's dynamic-table changelog modes directly as the comparison point for the stream-table duality, rather than reopening what a changelog mode is — the duality here is the same relationship from a library's, rather than a cluster's, point of view.

at.step: Setup: SQL formalised streams as tables, run by a cluster
